partially_covered.missing: Not all organization information is explicitly modeled (e.g., contact details, tax ID, legal form). Only address and global location number are present.
Mandatory identifier is modeled, but there is no explicit enumeration or SHACL/ontology-level restriction for all D96A-required fields. Logical consistency constraints are not formalized.

cq_coverage.details: The ontology covers nearly all CQs with clear classes and properties. Organization and file format validity details are only partially modeled, lacking some mandatory fields and constraints.

strengths: Rich class hierarchy reflecting EDIFACT structure
Good use of equivalence axioms for pivot classes
Functional properties and disjointness are well specified
weaknesses: No general class axioms (GCAs) for advanced validation
Some EDIFACT-required information not explicitly modeled (e.g., line item taxes, additional organization attributes)

likely_oops_pitfalls: P4 (Missing domain or range for some properties, if extended)
P7 (Lack of explicit inverse properties for all relations, though most are present)

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Expand the Organization class to include additional attributes such as tax ID, legal form, and contact information to fully answer CQ5.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables richer queries about organizations and increases CQ coverage.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model all mandatory D96A identifiers as explicit properties and add ontology-level cardinality/consistency constraints for file validity (CQ13).
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improves ability to validate file format compliance and enhances semantic interoperability.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Introduce general class axioms (GCAs) to express constraints such as the sum of line item prices equaling the invoice total, and mandatory presence of certain segments.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables advanced reasoning and validation, supporting SHACL integration.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Model taxes at the line item level and support for multiple tax rates/types.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Enables more granular queries and compliance with EN 16931-1.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Add additional roles (e.g., Seller, Payee) and support for parties beyond Buyer and Delivery Party.
improvement_suggestions.expected_impact: Improves extensibility for broader business scenarios.

summary: This ontology offers a robust and semantically rich model for EDIFACT invoices, with strong alignment to the competency questions and best practices in OWL 2. Its primary gaps are in the detailed modeling of organization information and explicit constraints for file validity, which can be addressed in the next iteration. Overall, it is well-structured and reasoner-friendly, with only minor areas for enhancement.
